policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'and suddenly there shone round about him a light out of heaven' carries the same words in either Greek order (ἐξαίφνης τε αὐτὸν περιήστραψεν / καὶ ἐξαίφνης περιήστραψεν αὐτόν); English word order is not evidence of Greek order and no note is mapped here.
ASV 'out of heaven' renders either ἐκ or ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ; the preposition choice is not distinguished by the English and no note is mapped.
ASV 'And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest' has no subject 'the Lord'; RP's added κύριος εἶπεν ('And the Lord said') is not rendered, so the ASV follows the shorter ὁ δέ.
ASV 'it shall be told thee what thou must do' renders ὅ τι, its orthographic form ὅτι, and simple τί alike as 'what'; the English does not distinguish them.
ASV 'And Saul arose' names Saul with or without the Greek article ὁ, which English proper names do not carry; the wording does not distinguish the readings.
ASV's opening 'And' carries either connective δέ or τε; the English does not distinguish them and no note is mapped.
ASV 'he saw nothing' renders the neuter οὐδέν; the masculine οὐδένα would give 'he saw no man', which the ASV does not read.
ASV 'the Lord said unto him in a vision' contains the same elements in either Greek order; English order is not evidence of Greek order.
ASV 'Arise, and go to the street' renders the coordinate participle ἀναστάς and the imperative ἀνάστα identically in this idiom; the English does not distinguish them.
ASV 'he hath seen a man named Ananias coming in' contains every element of both orders; the arrangement of ἄνδρα, ἐν ὁράματι, ὀνόματι and the name is not shown by the English.

ASV 'laying his hands on him' is plural, which excludes the singular χεῖρα (r02); anarthrous χεῖρας and articular τὰς χεῖρας both yield 'his hands' in English, so the remaining two are not distinguished.
ASV 'I have heard from many of this man' renders aorist ἤκουσα and perfect ἀκήκοα alike with the English present perfect; no note is mapped to distinguish them.
ASV 'how much evil he did to thy saints' contains verb and dative in the order English syntax requires; the Greek order of ἐποίησεν and τοῖς ἁγίοις σου is not shown.
ASV 'he is a chosen vessel unto me' carries both ἐστίν and μοι in either Greek order; the mapped note is a greek_gloss on 'chosen vessel' and does not touch this unit.
ASV 'before the Gentiles' takes the English definite article whether or not Greek τῶν is present; the wording does not distinguish anarthrous ἐθνῶν from τῶν ἐθνῶν.
ASV 'and the children of Israel' supplies the connective English requires to close the list, with or without Greek τε; the presence of the particle is not distinguished.
ASV 'the Lord, even Jesus, who appeared unto thee' renders the name Ἰησοῦς in apposition to ὁ κύριος; RP omits it and would give only 'the Lord'.
ASV 'there fell from his eyes' carries pronoun and prepositional phrase in either Greek order; English order is not evidence of Greek order.
ASV 'as it were scales' renders ὡς and ὡσεί alike; the English does not distinguish the two comparative particles.
ASV 'was strengthened' renders both intransitive active ἐνίσχυσεν and passive ἐνισχύθη, since English has no idiomatic intransitive active here; the voice is not distinguished.
ASV 'And he was certain days with the disciples' keeps the pronoun subject; RP's added ὁ Σαῦλος would name Saul, which the ASV does not do at this point.
ASV 'he proclaimed Jesus, that he is the Son of God' renders Ἰησοῦν; RP's χριστόν would give 'proclaimed the Christ'.
ASV 'that in Jerusalem made havoc of them' renders both ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ and εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ with 'in Jerusalem'; the preposition is not distinguished.
συνέχυννεν and συνέχυνεν are spellings of the same imperfect, both rendered 'confounded'; orthography leaves no trace in the English.
ASV 'the Jews that dwelt at Damascus' requires the English article regardless of Greek τούς; the presence of the article is not distinguished.
ASV 'And they watched the gates also day and night' renders the adverbial καί as 'also', present in παρετηροῦντο δὲ καί but absent from RP's παρετήρουν τε.
ASV 'his disciples took him by night' has the same elements as both orders; the position of αὐτόν relative to οἱ μαθηταί is not shown by the English.
ASV 'let him down through the wall' carries verb, prepositional phrase and object in English order; the Greek arrangement is not distinguished.
ASV 'And when he was come to Jerusalem' keeps a pronoun subject; RP's ὁ Σαῦλος ἐν would name Saul, which the ASV does not.
ASV 'he assayed to join himself to the disciples' renders ἐπείραζεν and ἐπειρᾶτο alike; the English shows no difference of stem or voice here.
ASV 'in the name of Jesus' is unaffected by the Greek article τοῦ before the name; the wording does not distinguish its presence.
ASV 'going in and going out at Jerusalem' renders both participles; RP omits καὶ ἐκπορευόμενος and would leave only 'going in'.
ASV runs 'at Jerusalem,' straight into 'preaching boldly in the name of the Lord' with no connective; RP's added καί would give 'and preaching boldly'.
ASV 'in the name of the Lord' stops at κυρίου; RP's added Ἰησοῦ would give 'of the Lord Jesus'.
ASV 'they were seeking to kill him' places object after verb as English requires; the Greek order of ἀνελεῖν and αὐτόν is not shown, and the mapped note glosses 'Grecian Jews' only.

ASV 'the church ... had peace, being edified ... was multiplied' is singular throughout, which excludes RP's plural αἱ ἐκκλησίαι ... ἐπληθύνοντο (r02); the base lemma and r01 are the same singular text, so the English does not distinguish between them.
ASV 'a certain man named Aeneas' carries both ὀνόματι and the name in either Greek order; English order is not evidence of Greek order.
ASV 'who had kept his bed eight years' renders the noun without showing its spelling or case; κραβάττου and κραββάτῳ are alike absorbed by the English idiom.
ASV 'Jesus Christ healeth thee' treats Χριστός as a name, which the Greek article ὁ does not alter in English; the readings are not distinguished.
ASV 'and in Sharon' transliterates Σαρῶνα; RP's Ἀσσάρωνα would yield 'Assaron', which the ASV does not read.
ASV 'full of good works' fixes adjective before noun by English rule; the Greek order of ἔργων and ἀγαθῶν is not distinguished, and the mapped note explains 'Dorcas' only.
ASV 'they laid her in an upper chamber' renders the object αὐτήν, which excludes WH's ἔθηκαν without it (r02); the two readings that keep αὐτήν differ only in order, which the English does not show.
ASV 'sent two men unto him' renders δύο ἄνδρας; RP omits the phrase and would give only 'sent unto him'.

ASV reports the message as direct address, 'entreating him, Delay not to come on unto us', which requires the subjunctive prohibition μὴ ὀκνήσῃς; RP's infinitive ὀκνῆσαι gives indirect discourse ('that he would not delay').
ASV 'to come on unto us' is first person, rendering ἡμῶν; RP's αὐτῶν would give 'unto them'.
ASV strings this verse with connectives English narrative supplies of itself ('and kneeled down, and prayed; and turning'); none of them fixes whether this particular καί stood in the Greek.
ASV 'throughout all Joppa' takes no English article before the place name whether or not Greek τῆς is present; the readings are not distinguished.
ASV 'and many believed on the Lord' puts subject before verb as English requires; the Greek order of ἐπίστευσαν and πολλοί is not shown.
ASV 'that he abode many days in Joppa' supplies the subject of the infinitive as English requires, whether or not αὐτόν stood in the Greek; the reading is not distinguished.
ASV 'that he abode many days' equally supplies the accusative subject of μεῖναι; the presence of αὐτόν after the infinitive leaves no trace in the English.
